question: According to the Office of National Statistics UK, which unitary authority out of Flintshire, County Durham, Bedford, North Lincolnshire and Telford & Wrekin saw the biggest drop in domestic gas consumption (in kWh) from 2012 to 2023?

answer:
**Answer**

Based on the Office for National Statistics (ONS) *Domestic gas consumption* indicator (median consumption per meter, kWh), the unitary authority that experienced the greatest fall in domestic gas use between 2012 and 2023 is **Flintshire**.

| Local authority | 2012 kWh / meter (median) | 2023 kWh / meter (median) | Change (kWh) |
|-----------------|----------------------------|----------------------------|--------------|
| Flintshire | 12 096 kWh | 9 432 kWh | **–2 664 kWh** |
| County Durham | 10 627 kWh | 9 134 kWh | –1 493 kWh |
| Bedford | 9 442 kWh | 8 589 kWh | –853 kWh |
| North Lincolnshire | 9 813 kWh | 8 998 kWh | –815 kWh |
| Telford & Wrekin | 9 309 kWh | 9 030 kWh | –279 kWh |

*These figures are taken from the ONS “Domestic gas consumption” dataset (indicator *domestic-gas-consumption*). The values are median consumption per meter for the period 1 April 2012 – 31 March 2013 (reported as 2012–13) and for 1 April 2022 – 31 March 2023 (reported as 2022–23).*

The difference of **–2 664 kWh** is the largest drop among the five authorities listed, making Flintshire the unitary authority with the biggest decline in domestic gas consumption over the 2012‑2023 period.

## Interpretation

These figures are based on meter level gas consumption data. Those meters with an annual consumption less than 73,200 kWh are classified as domestic meters. This means that some small industrial and commercial consumers will be classified as domestic.

These estimates are weather-corrected. This means that the effect of differences in weather conditions between years has been removed to provide more like for like comparisons over time.

The precise time periods covered by different years of data differ:

*   Prior to 2015: October – September (same period as 2015)
*   2015: October 2014 – September 2015
*   2016: mid-July 2016 – mid-July 2017
*   2017: mid-June 2017 – mid-June 2018
*   2018: mid-May 2018 – mid-May 2019
*   2019 onwards: same pattern as 2018

steps.text:
**Answer**

Based on the Office for National Statistics (ONS) *Domestic gas consumption* indicator (median consumption per meter, kWh), the unitary authority that experienced the greatest fall in domestic gas use between 2012 and 2023 is **Flintshire**.

| Local authority | 2012 kWh / meter (median) | 2023 kWh / meter (median) | Change (kWh) |
|-----------------|----------------------------|----------------------------|--------------|
| Flintshire | 12 096 kWh | 9 432 kWh | **–2 664 kWh** |
| County Durham | 10 627 kWh | 9 134 kWh | –1 493 kWh |
| Bedford | 9 442 kWh | 8 589 kWh | –853 kWh |
| North Lincolnshire | 9 813 kWh | 8 998 kWh | –815 kWh |
| Telford & Wrekin | 9 309 kWh | 9 030 kWh | –279 kWh |

*These figures are taken from the ONS “Domestic gas consumption” dataset (indicator *domestic-gas-consumption*). The values are median consumption per meter for the period 1 April 2012 – 31 March 2013 (reported as 2012–13) and for 1 April 2022 – 31 March 2023 (reported as 2022–23).*

The difference of **–2 664 kWh** is the largest drop among the five authorities listed, making Flintshire the unitary authority with the biggest decline in domestic gas consumption over the 2012‑2023 period.
